name: Statistical Inference
description: Basic concepts and data visualization: measures of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, kurtosis, data representation using histogram, pie chart, boxplot, biplot; revision of probability distribution: some standard discrete and continuous distributions; some standard probability inequalities; order statistics: different order statistics and their single and joint distribution; mode of convergence, CLT; random number generation: generation of random numbers following certain distributions; sampling distribution of mean, variance; emphasis on normal, chi-square, student's t, F distributions; theory of estimation: properties of an estimator, sufficient, completeness, minimal sufficient, ancillarity, unbiased estimator, MVUE, BLUE, Fisher information, Cramer-Rao inequality, Rao-Blackwell theorem, Lehmann-Scheffé theorem; methods of finding estimators: MoM, MLE; testing of hypothesis: mean and variance, Neyman-Pearson lemma, MLR, Karlin-Rubin theorem, LRT; non-parametric methods run tests, rank tests, signed rank tests, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, chi-squared goodness of fit test, test of homogeneity, test of independence, etc.; confidence interval estimation: inversion of a test procedure, pivotal approach; methods of evaluating interval estimation.
